Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Time, the calendar & feasts

three quarters of an hour noun

also forty-five minutes, a quarter to, quarter to

classical

Plin. NH 18.219: dōdrāns hōrae
Plin. NH 2.58: dōdrantēs sēmunciās hōrārum
Traupman 330

dōdrāns hōrae

The noun is dōdrāns, dōdrantis m.

Examples

  • Est prīma hōra et dōdrāns.

    It’s a quarter to two (1:45: one o’clock and three quarters).Traupman 81

  • hōrā duodēvīcēsimā et dōdrante jūs facitō

    at a quarter to six in the evening (17:45), make the gravyCulīna Theodōrī

See also twelfth, telling the time, quarter of an hour, hour.

SourcesLewis & Short: dodrans

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 81, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).: p. 330.

Theodōrus et pater: Culīna Theodōrī, the recipe book that goes with the libellī (Ad Libellōs I–VII); examples marked “Culīna Theodōrī” quote it word for word.
